questions.question: If a trailer starts to jackknife, you should NOT:

options.text: Let the wheels grip the road.

questions.explanation: If a trailer jackknifes, release the brakes and let the wheels grip the road again. Do not apply the trailer hand brake because it will make the skid worse. Brakes cause the wheels to lock in the first place.

questions.question: Starting in what year were new trailers required to have ABS?
questions.explanation: All trailers made after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: A lightly-loaded combination vehicle stops more slowly than a fully-loaded vehicle because:

options.text: Stiff suspension springs and strong brakes give high traction.
Stiff suspension springs and strong brakes give low traction.
Brakes only work when a trailer reaches a minimum weight.
Suspension springs only work when a trailer reaches a minimum weight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stiff suspension springs and strong brakes give low traction.
questions.explanation: An empty combination vehicle takes longer to stop than a fully-loaded vehicle. Stiff suspension springs and strong brakes provide less traction on a light trailer than on a loaded trailer.

questions.question: When driving a bobtail tractor, know that:

options.text: Bobtails cannot drive as fast as tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with trailers.
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a trailer attached. Stopping a bobtail is difficult and takes a longer distance than stopping a tractor with a loaded trailer.

questions.question: Rollovers happen when drivers:
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers take turns at too high a speed. Take turns and curves slowly and safely.

questions.question: In a double or triple combination:

options.text: Cargo weight must be split equally between all trailers.
The heaviest trailer should be right behind the cab.
The heaviest trailer should be in the rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The heaviest trailer should be right behind the cab.
questions.explanation: The heaviest trailer should be closest to the tractor. The lightest trailer should be in the rear.

questions.question: When lightly loaded, combination vehicles:

options.text: Should have most weight in the rear of the trailer.

questions.explanation: When a combination vehicle is lightly loaded, it has poor traction. Wheels lock up easily when stopping a lightly-loaded vehicle.

questions.question: Using the trailer hand valve while driving:
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve while driving. It can cause your trailer to skid.

questions.question: If oil and water build up in your air tanks, the brakes:
questions.explanation: Drain air tanks daily to remove water and oil. Too much oil and water in the air tanks can damage the brakes.

questions.question: Before driving, make sure air reaches all trailers by:

options.text: Opening the rear shut-off valves and listening for air.
Closing the rear shut-off valves and listening for air.
Disconnecting air supply lines and listening for air.
Rolling each trailer down a hill and testing the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening the rear shut-off valves and listening for air.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check that air reaches all trailers. Let air pressure build up, then send air to the emergency and service lines. Open the shut-off valves at the rear of the last trailer. If air escapes, air is reaching the entire vehicle.

questions.question: What is another name for the service line?
questions.explanation: The service line is also called the control line. It carries air to the trailer brakes. You control it with the foot brake or trailer hand brake.

questions.question: Large combination vehicles take the longest time to stop when:
questions.explanation: Empty vehicles take longer to stop than loaded ones. Less weight means less grip between the wheels and the road.

questions.question: How can you avoid making sudden lane changes?

options.text: Use your horn to make other drivers move out of your lane.
Drive slower than the posted speed limit.
Look ahead at the road while driving.
Pull off the road and wait when traffic is heavy.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead at the road while driving.
questions.explanation: Sudden lane changes are dangerous with combination vehicles. Look down the road ahead to spot obstacles. This gives you time to plan your moves instead of making sudden changes.

questions.question: Combination vehicles:

options.text: Are usually shorter than single commercial vehicles.
Are usually lighter than single commercial vehicles.
Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
Are easier to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are heavier and longer than single commercial vehicles. Because of this, they require more driving skill.

questions.question: Driving a combination vehicle ____ than driving a single vehicle.
questions.explanation: Driving a combination vehicle requires more skill than driving a single vehicle. Combination vehicles are longer and heavier than single commercial vehicles.

questions.question: To prevent a rollover, cargo should be:

options.text: Placed near the front of a trailer.
Placed near the rear of a trailer.
Loaded with most weight on the driver's side of a trailer.

questions.explanation: To reduce rollover risk, spread cargo evenly across the trailer. Keep the weight centered and as low to the ground as possible.

questions.question: Rollovers happen when:
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers take turns too fast.

questions.question: The service air line is attached to the:
questions.explanation: The service air line is attached to relay valves. These valves let the trailer brakes apply quickly when you use the foot brake or trailer hand brake.

questions.question: Rollovers are most likely to happen when:
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn too fast. Slow down before entering turns and curves, especially when your rig is fully loaded.

questions.question: ____ cause more than half of all accident-related truck driver deaths.
questions.explanation: More than half of all accident-related truck driver deaths result from truck rollovers. To prevent rollovers, load cargo low and centered. Take corners slowly and carefully.
